instruction: We are planning a get-together with our friends next week. Buy stuff according to the checklist my husband sent me over email.
notes: The checklist is modeled as a file attachment on the husband's email: the agent searches the inbox (query 'checklist'), opens the thread to get the attachment id, logs into file_system, downloads the attachment (needs both tokens) and reads it with show_file, which makes (checklist-read) true. The checklist is assumed to list Amazon product ids with quantities (private data key checklist_product_id_to_quantity); 5 items are assumed (product-i/quantity-i objects, bound at runtime from the file content) - adjust the number of product/quantity/count objects and checklist-size if the actual list differs. The cart is cleared first so the order contains exactly the checklist items; each add_product_to_cart consumes one checklist entry (on-checklist, not yet added) and advances a count chain, and place_order requires the count to equal checklist-size, the home address (home-address) and a known payment card, so (order-placed) is reachable only after every checklist item has been added with its quantity. Adding items after the order is forbidden via (not (order-placed)). The count parameters of add-product-to-cart/place-order are pure bookkeeping (not API arguments). Goal is (order-placed) and (task-completed); complete_task takes no answer.
